/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report - 11 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2959 (97)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4700 (243)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2103 (28)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1810 (4)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1036 (5)

CAPESIZE
The Capesize market enjoyed a positive session today, with the BCI 182 5TC climbing by $2,208 to $42,628. The Pacific led the advance, with the C5 index jumping $1.030 to $14.620, while C3 was comparatively unchanged, registering only a marginal dip of $0.077 to $36.209. Activity in the Pacific picked up, with two miners active, although the move in rates was considerably more pronounced. Owners held firm from the outset, generally indicating in the upper $14s, while one miner opened with bids at $13.30 before gradually improving to $13.50. With owners remaining confident in the mid to upper $14s, the market eventually saw a couple of fixtures concluded at $14.40 and $14.50. There were also rumours of a second miner paying $14.80, although this was subsequently denied. In the Atlantic, conditions appeared to be finding a degree of stability in the South Atlantic, with some owners reportedly pulling offers back towards the upper $36s as bids gradually edged into the mid to upper $35s. Meanwhile, sentiment remained positive in the North Atlantic, where activity improved at better levels. With the Pacific taking a sizeable step forward and the North Atlantic continuing to provide support, the overall market finished on a firm note.

PANAMAX
The Atlantic continued to demonstrate a firm undertone today, with further improvements across the routes, although brokers suggested that the pace of recent gains could begin to moderate as additional tonnage becomes available. In the North Atlantic, prompt trans-Atlantic requirements continued to attract firmer levels, particularly for November dates, while charterers looking further into December appeared to have greater flexibility and were consequently less inclined to chase higher levels. Fronthaul enquiry remained present, although charterers were said to appear increasingly selective at current levels. Further south, EC South America continued to benefit from a favourable tonnage balance for late November and early December, with owners showing little appetite to entertain lower bids. A widening bid-offer spread was reported, whilst concluded fixture levels continued to improve. In the Pacific, market participants reported a reasonable flow of fresh cargoes from Australia and Indonesia, although an increase in available tonnage prevented this from translating into firmer rates. With charterers adopting a more patient approach, recent gains appeared difficult to maintain. A number of vessels were reported on subjects, including the Pedhoulas Fighter (82,994 2024) Panjin 9 November and ETG Mishima (81,957 2021) Tomogashima 15 November, both for Australian round trips, while the CK Angie (81,147 2011) Zhoushan 13 November was linked to a North Pacific round voyage. Elsewhere, the Myrtos Bay (82,000 2026) Zhoushan 14 November, Yasa Diamond (84,989 2021) CJK 14 November and Gallia Graeca II (82,769 2025) Nansha 16 November were also reported on subjects, with further details yet to emerge. Period activity was also evident, with the Ormos (81,944 2019) Tianjin 14 November reportedly placed on subjects for 5–7 months at around $20,500. The P5TC advanced $251 to close at $18,923.

SUPRAMAX
The 11TC average was positive again for the first time in 2 weeks, rising $49 to $22,877, mainly driven by the jump in US Gulf rates which dominated the day’s rumour mill. The morning started with reports of the
Anatoli (63,467 2018) open New Orleans 12-13 November being on subjects for a trip Far East with grains at around $29/30,000 with Norden and the African Hammerkop (63,526 2024) Houston 18 November also being on subjects for a trip India with coal at $36,000 with Oldendorff. Norden were also linked with the BCH Bramberg (63,167 2015) open Quebec 16 November for a woodpellets cargo from Chesapeake to UK-Continent at $35,000, whilst Ultrabulk placed the Misago Arrow (62,823 2015) open Mobile on subjects basis delivery US Gulf again for woodpellets to UK-Continent at $27,000. There was talk of a 64,000-dwt fixed from US Gulf to North coast South America with grains at $24,000, although further details didn’t materialize, and Aries Bulk reportedly took the Lila (63,414 2017) open Houston 19-22 November for a trip to India intention petcoke at $34,000. Despite a large jump in transatlantic rates, the afternoon surprised many with talk of the Unity Discovery (60,629 2017) being on subjects Mississippi River to East Mediterranean with petcoke at either $40,000 or $42,000 with Nova Levantina, and there was also talk of the Chise (64,678 2022) being on subjects on voyage basis for another petcoke stem with Trammo from US Gulf to the East Mediterranean at the equivalent of $45,500. Whilst North America made the headlines, the South Atlantic continued improving with vessels fixing above last done, with the Continent and Mediterranean markets largely unchanged in light trading. In Asia rates continue to soften slightly with a lack of fresh NoPac enquiry to support the backhaul market, whilst South East Asia is still affected by ballasters from the Indian Ocean, with larger types switching their attention to the Australian market instead with better returns on offer.

HANDYSIZE
It was a relatively active day for the sector, with overall sentiment remaining positive. The BHSI closed at 1,036, while the 7TC average gained $85 to reach $18,645. Market conditions across the Continent and Mediterranean remained largely unchanged, with rates holding steady. In contrast, the US Gulf and South Atlantic continued to see a pickup in fresh demand, with firm sentiment pushing rates above previous levels. Meanwhile, the Asian market remained resilient, supported by a shortage of tonnage in the North Pacific.

Atlantic
The Matilda GS (33,407 2016) was placed on subjects by Centrurion for a trip with delivery West Palm Beach via Barcarena to Tunisia at around $18,000–$19,000. The African Rail (39,784 2015) was fixed by LDC on voyage terms for an inter-Caribbean trip, although further details were not disclosed. In addition, a 35,000-dwt vessel was fixed by WBC for a trip from SW Pass to the UK–Continent, including Denmark, with wood pellets at $18,000. A 34,000-dwt vessel was fixed by NBC for a trip from Tuzla via the Black Sea to NC South America with steels at $13,750. Further details of these fixtures were not disclosed.

Asia
The Ocean Happiness (37,572 2017) open Penang was placed on subjects on a dop basis for an Australia round trip in the mid-to-high $17,000s, although further details were not disclosed.
